questions.q: Why do scratch orgs specifically need a repeatable, version-controlled approach to seeding sample data?
options: Because Salesforce prohibits entering data manually into any scratch org
Because scratch orgs cannot run SOQL queries
Because a scratch org starts empty and is routinely deleted or expires within days, so manually re-entering data every time isn't sustainable
Because sf data commands only work on scratch orgs, never on sandboxes
questions.explain: Scratch orgs are disposable by design (Lesson 5) — they get deleted or expire within days, so relying on manual data entry every time one is recreated doesn't scale; a repeatable, version-controlled data plan solves this.

questions.q: What format does `sf data export tree` write exported records to?
options: The sObject tree format — nested JSON structured around parent-child records with a single root type
A CSV file with one row per record, flattened
A raw Metadata API zip file
questions.explain: sf data export tree writes matching records as JSON in the sObject tree format, a nested structure built around parent-child relationships rooted at a single record type.

questions.q: What does the --plan flag add when exporting data that spans more than one related object?
options: It increases the per-query record limit beyond 2,000
It produces one JSON file per object plus a plan definition file that preserves the parent-child relationships for re-import
It automatically deletes the source org's data after export
It converts the export into CSV format instead of JSON
questions.explain: --plan generates a separate JSON file per object involved, plus a plan definition file (ending -plan.json) that ties them together and preserves relationships between records from different objects when later imported.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of records a single sf data export tree query can return?
questions.explain: A single export query can return at most 2,000 records — these commands are designed for small sample datasets (Salesforce frames the overall use case as under roughly 3,000 records), not large-scale data migration.

questions.q: If you import individual exported files directly with --files instead of using a generated plan, what are you responsible for?
options: Nothing — ordering is handled automatically regardless of how you import
Manually renaming each file to match the target org's object API names
Listing the files in the correct parent-before-child order yourself, since there's no plan file doing that ordering for you
Re-running sf org create shape before every import
questions.explain: Without a plan file handling the ordering, importing related files with --files requires you to list them yourself in the correct parent-before-child order so relationships resolve correctly.
